routes.serves: note list JSON that feeds the home page notes area (pinned notes and regular notes)
create a note from the Take a note editor (title + content); returns 201 with the created note, 400 on invalid JSON body
update an existing note's labels (and title/content/color/reminder); returns 200 with the updated note, 404 when the note does not exist, 400 on invalid JSON body
soft-delete a note (moves it to the Trash); returns 200 with the note, 404 when missing
restore a deleted note from the Trash; returns 200 with the note, 404 when missing
archive or unarchive a note; returns 200 with the updated note, 404 when the note does not exist
pin or unpin a note; returns 200 with the updated note, 404 when the note does not exist
permanently delete a note from the Trash view; returns 200 with the note, 404 when missing
empty the trash; returns 200 with the removed count

notes: REQ-2.7.6.1 (filter the notes list by a selected label) is satisfied by the label-filter mechanism built for REQ-2.7.1, which this node depends on. The sidebar (opened via the 'Main menu' button) renders one label-filter button per catalog label ('Work', 'Reminders', 'Work editable'); each button carries the exact accessible name (icon is aria-hidden, text node is the label name). Clicking a label sets state.labelFilter and switches the view to the notes list; visibleInView() then shows only notes whose labels array includes the selected label, so the notes list shows only notes that have the selected label. Fixtures: the system contains the regular note 'Design review' with the 'Work' label and the regular note 'Movie list' with no 'Work'/'Reminders' label (both seeded in backend/data/db.json and rendered as note cards with title text). Clicking 'Work' therefore shows 'Design review' and hides 'Movie list'. No new routes or backend changes are required: the filter is pure client state (state.labelFilter) over the existing GET /api/notes payload, so parallel test files sharing one server never observe each other's filters. The label catalog is per-page-load client state (let LABEL_CATALOG), restored on every fresh load.
